terra.problem: The mixed-up dough joke has no clear payoff: it doesn't explain what was mixed up or how the oven revealed it.
“Wrong crown” uses “wrong” about the baker's answer.
The passage doesn't say Zedekiah started the day in Jerusalem.
“Wrong direction” uses “wrong” about the baker's answer.
The explanation says people lamented for the earlier kings in the same way. The verse compares the burning of spices, but doesn't say the earlier kings were lamented in those words.
“A whole kingdom is standing” suggests Judah was intact, which the passage doesn't say.
The joke about sampling dough makes light of the people breaking their covenant and forcing others back into slavery. The lock comparison is also unclear.
“Third is too soon” suggests that releasing a servant earlier was forbidden. The passage doesn't say that.
The passage names the house that bears the LORD's Name; it doesn't rule out a courtyard as such.
“No boss attached” adds a condition the text doesn't state. It says they were free to go wherever they wanted.
